content.text:
**Observations**

- The W1 rows fall into two clear populations: "untouched" rows whose 16 values all lie within about ±0.036 (the PyTorch default init range for fan‑in 784, i.e. pixels that were essentially never non‑zero in training), and "touched" rows with values up to ±0.4. The touched/untouched pattern repeats with period 28, confirming row‑major 28×28 layout.
- Untouched pixels: all of image row 0 except columns 12–15; columns 0–1 and 24–27 of rows 1–4; columns 0–3 and 24–27 of row 27; corners generally. Everything else — from row 1 down to row 27 and from column ~1 to column 27 — carries trained weights. So the objects fill essentially the whole 28×28 frame, touching the top edge (centre), the bottom edge (cols 4–23), the left edge (col 0–1 in rows ~6–25) and the right edge (cols 25–27 in rows 3–7 and 23–26).
- The *largest* weights sit on the periphery rather than the centre: image rows 1–3 (cols 4–24, |w| up to 0.4, e.g. unit 1 strongly +, units 2/4/7/10/14 strongly −), rows 25–27 (units 4, 5 strongly +, unit 14 strongly −), the left edge col 0–1 in lower‑middle rows (units 0, 12, 15, 10 +; units 3, 7, 11, 14 −), and the upper‑right corner rows 3–7 cols 22–27 (units 3, 6, 10 +; units 4, 15 −). Centre‑image weights are moderate (0.1–0.2). This says the network mainly reads the *silhouette/extent* of the object: does it reach the top, does it reach the bottom, does it stick out to the left/right.
- Some units show horizontal structure: unit 14 is positive in a horizontal band in the middle rows and negative at top and bottom (a wide, low object vs. a tall one); unit 0 is positive in the central columns of the lower‑middle rows while unit 9 has two lateral lobes with a negative centre (presence vs. absence of mass in the centre column).
- Output layer: the "top‑of‑image" unit 1 feeds negatively into classes 4, 5, 7, 9 and positively into 2, 3, 6, 8; the "bottom‑rows" unit 5 feeds +1.04 into class 9 and −1.43 into class 4; the "centre‑columns" unit 0 feeds −1.59 into class 1 and +1.17 into class 2; the upper‑right‑corner units (3, 6, 10, −15) feed positively into classes 4 and 9; left‑edge units sum strongly positive for class 2. Biases: class 8 has a large negative bias (−0.77), class 5 a large positive one (+0.56).

**Reasoning**

- MNIST, EMNIST and (to a lesser extent) KMNIST place the glyph in a centred 20×20 box with centre‑of‑mass alignment, so rows 0–3, rows 24–27, columns 0–3 and 24–27 are (almost) always zero and their weights would stay at init. Here those border pixels are not only touched but carry some of the largest weights in the network, so handwritten‑digit/letter datasets are ruled out. Handwritten characters would also make the centre, not the frame edges, the most informative region.
- Full‑frame photographs (e.g. sign‑language or face crops) would leave no untouched pixels at all; here corners and most of row 0 are untouched, so the images are objects on a black background, scaled to fill the frame.
- Fashion‑MNIST fits exactly: items are rescaled so the longest side spans all 28 pixels and are centred, so tall items (trousers, dresses) touch rows 0 and 27 near the centre, wide items (shoes, bags, outstretched sleeves) touch columns 0 and 27 in the middle rows, and the top rows are empty only for footwear. The output‑layer signs match the Fashion‑MNIST label order: "content at the top" votes against 5, 7, 9 (sandal, sneaker, ankle boot); "mass in the centre column" votes against 1 (trouser — gap between the legs); bottom‑row mass helps 9 (boot) and hurts 4 (coat); upper‑right content helps 4 (right shoulder/sleeve of a coat) and 9 (boot shaft); left‑edge content strongly helps 2 (long sleeves of a pullover).
- The scattered single‑pixel spikes/dips near the top (e.g. (2,12) very strong, (1,12) untouched) look like small‑sample/overfitting artefacts rather than dataset structure.

**Dataset**

Fashion‑MNIST (Zalando 28×28 grayscale clothing items, white object on black background).

**Classes**

0 T‑shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence**

65%
